frus-1864p4:
The 1864 papers close with Part IV and a scatter of smaller powers. Spain takes the first and longest section. Austria, Chile, and Prussia follow. Belgium and Portugal have substantial files. Italy, Denmark, and Sweden and Norway appear. Turkey, Switzerland, Egypt, Morocco, and Tunis round out the volume. A short supplement returns to Great Britain.

Spain's papers turn on sea law and the Caribbean. Maritime jurisdiction heads the first letters. Santo Domingo and the slave trade recur. Seward watches Cuba for signs of revolt. The Prussian file catches Europe's own war. Reports from Berlin describe the fighting at Düppel and in Jutland. Even minor posts felt the war's pull. The volume completes a year of global vigilance.
frus-1865p4:
This appendix to the 1865 correspondence gathers the world's response to a murder. Lincoln was shot on the evening of April 14, 1865. William Seward and his son Frederick were attacked the same night. Governments across the globe sent condolences. This volume prints them country by country. Austria and the Argentine Republic open the list.

France and Great Britain fill the largest blocks. Paris press extracts follow the French letters. British papers run for hundreds of documents. Italy, Prussia, and Spain send formal addresses. Small states, cities, and Sunday school unions also write. Switzerland alone supplies a long run of messages. The book is less diplomacy than public mourning. It shows Lincoln's standing far beyond America.
podcast-joerogan-ysuqhQErnp4:
Jeffrey Epstein's links to the world of science are examined in this Joe Rogan Experience segment. Epstein, a wealthy financier and convicted sex offender, funded researchers and courted famous labs and universities. His money bought him access to some of the brightest names in science.

Rogan and his guest go through which institutions took his donations and what they gave in return. They ask why so many smart people stayed close to a man with a known record. The talk mixes money, power, and moral failure in equal parts. Listeners disturbed by the case get a focused look at one of its least examined corners.
